title: Exeter, Summerland Street: RIBA Stage 2 outline fire strategy for a co-living block (BS 9991 variations)
jurisdiction: England, UK (Exeter, Devon). COMPARATIVE NON-ALBERTA RECORD; UK Building Regulations framing retained; no Alberta applicability asserted.
code_edition: Building Regulations 2010 (England). BS 9991:2015 incorporating Corrigendum No.1 stated as principal guidance (p.4, s.1.2.2). Approved Document B edition not stated; text refers to 'ADB Vol 1' and to anticipated ADB amendments (p.12).

facts.text: Orion Fire Engineering was appointed by McLaren Properties to produce a RIBA Stage 2 outline fire strategy for the Summerland Street residential development in Exeter, as a basis for the design team; the text calls it a 'pre-planning fire strategy'.

Principal guidance is BS 9991:2015 (incorporating Corrigendum No.1). The building is six storeys of co-living accommodation, footprint 1,150 m2, maximum occupied storey height 17.6 m, and is 'designed as a block of flats' for guidance purposes.

The design basis is fourteen architectural drawings by Stride Treglown (site, floor, roof, elevation and section drawings, revisions S2_P18 to S2_P32, dated 29/08/2023). The report states that revisions to those drawings 'may invalidate this report'.

Table 2 lists four variations from BS 9991: natural smoke shafts close to the stair on Levels 1-4 (subject to Building Control Body discussion); the eastern protected stair as the single means of escape from dwellings at Level 5, connected to ground-floor ancillary accommodation ('may be justified in further detail at RIBA Stage 3'); ancillary rooms opening off single-direction residential corridors; and a Level 5 single-direction travel distance above 15 m (below 30 m) compensated by mechanical smoke ventilation 'subject to BCB approval at a later design stage'.

Table 3 lists further works for RIBA Stage 3, including 'Discuss the variations to prescriptive guidance within this report with the approval authorities', and states that the architect's GA plans 'will need to be developed alongside this pre-planning fire strategy'.

Several provisions are labelled a 'design risk' pending agreement with approval bodies: smoke ingress into a stair (p.10), a single-stair dwelling corridor connected to ancillary areas (p.15, s.4.2.9) and a ground-floor connection through a lift lobby (p.16, s.4.2.11).
The text repeatedly refers to items 'highlighted in Appendix A' (drawing comments). In this PDF, Appendix A is a divider page only; the marked drawings are not included.
facts.locator: references on p.7, p.8, p.14-p.17; appendix divider p.22

facts.text: For external walls, the report recommends Class A2-s1,d0 at a minimum, with insulation and filler materials also restricted, 'to mitigate the impact of anticipated changes in Approved Document B'.

The report states that no fire safety requirements apply beyond Part B 'with the exception of Class A1 insulation materials in the external wall build-up', and asks to be advised of any client, insurer or warranty requirement that changes this.

Fire service access: a dry riser serves both protected stairs and the appliance must be able to park within 18 m of both. The three adjacent public roads are said to meet the pump appliance dimensions, subject to consultation with the fire authority and Building Control.
Figures 8-11 (relevant boundary, external wall protected areas for the ground floor and Levels 1-5, and fire service provisions) are embedded as drawings in the PDF.
